criterion_scores.reasoning: The patch does the intended core job: build_graph filters ignored files, the generator drops ignored nodes/edges, and the verifier fails when a gitignored path is found. I checked the fail-closed/error paths and edge-dst handling. The remaining issue is the over-broad prefilter that can skip absolute or `~`-prefixed paths, which is a minor correctness gap.

The two required defenses are present: pipeline-side exclusion and hub-side enforcement in pnpm check. I also checked the skip note for missing pipeline checkout. The implementation is slightly narrow because the verifier only scans the visible node/edge fields, not an exhaustive walk of every possible path-bearing field in the JSON artifact.

No house-convention violations are visible in this diff: no wrong skill naming, no secret handling issue, and the new checks are wired in the expected public-hub/pipeline locations. I checked placement, naming, and the guarded-write path expectations I could verify from the snippet.

This is a lean defense-in-depth change rather than extra abstraction. It avoids the tombstoned patterns called out in the rubric and does not introduce duplicated state beyond the necessary verification pass. I did not find speculative surface or ceremony that looks load-bearing.

The new comments and log messages are specific about what is being blocked or skipped, and the verifier reports the pipeline checkout case clearly. I checked for silent failure modes and overclaiming; the main remaining nit is that the privacy guard’s path filtering is not explained as a deliberate exclusion of absolute/tilde paths.

defects.description: This silently drops absolute and `~`-prefixed paths from the privacy check instead of failing closed. If a bad path form ever reaches the generator, it can evade the git-ignore guard rather than being rejected.

defects.spec_ref: YED-236 requirement: fail if any gitignored path appears in system-map.files.json
defects.description: The verifier only inspects node ids and edge endpoints. That covers the current visible schema, but it is not an exhaustive scan of `system-map.files.json`, so any future or hidden path-bearing field in the same file would bypass the guard.

checks_performed: Checked the build_graph.py change for whether ignored paths are removed before indexing and whether ignored references are treated as absent.
Checked the gen-system-map.mjs change for fail-closed behavior around git check-ignore, path normalization/filtering, and whether both node ids and edge endpoints are screened.
Checked the verify-system-map.mjs change for whether pnpm check fails on gitignored paths and whether the no-pipeline-checkout path is handled as a skip-with-note.
Checked for remaining leak paths in the shown outputs (nodes, edges, and any other visible path-bearing fields in system-map.files.json).
Checked the supplied spec for numbered decisions; none were present, so I judged against the stated YED-236 requirements directly.
